key_insight: Two structure-preserving discretisations generate entropy and enforce quasi-incompressibility pointwise, while the continuous Petrov–Galerkin method also conserves total energy.
engineering_relevance: These methods support physically consistent simulation of miscible multicomponent flows with coupled thermal, diffusion, and momentum effects.
method: Formulate the thermal Maxwell–Stefan–Navier–Stokes system using an entropy balance.
Combine semi-implicit Euler time stepping with suitable spatial finite elements.
Use continuous Petrov–Galerkin time discretisation for energy conservation and high-order temporal approximation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments demonstrate the structure-preserving properties and behaviour of both methods, but the abstract reports no quantitative accuracy or performance metrics.
watch_item: The semi-implicit Euler method numerically dissipates total energy despite preserving entropy generation and the quasi-incompressibility constraint.
paper_title: Structure-preserving discretisations for the quasi-incompressible, thermal Maxwell-Stefan equations
